conflicts: Real-world figures are spreads from several sources and are kept side by side, never averaged; the maker interval is always given with them.
not_found: Brake pad life in hours: no public engine-builder, magazine or two-agreeing owner source with hour figures was found; makers say inspect every race and replace as required.
Wheel bearing and linkage/swingarm bearing replacement hours: makers publish inspection and greasing intervals only; no two agreeing public real-world hour figures were found.
Spark plug real-world life: makers publish intervals (e.g. Kawasaki 7.5 h, KTM two-strokes 15 h); no independent hour figures found.

Honda CRF450R/CRF250R 2020-on and Kawasaki KX450/KX250 2020-on: no two agreeing public reports with hours for how often the valves actually tighten on these generations (older-generation Honda titanium-valve reports exist but do not apply). Some owner-forum pages could not be read and were not used.

records.statement: KTM and Husqvarna schedule a new piston at the minor engine service every 50 operating hours, with valves and con-rod at the major service every 100 hours. An engine shop that builds motocross and enduro engines publishes 15-30 hours for 250F and 450F pistons and rings in race use, and notes modern makers ask for a piston at about 15 hours or 5-6 races. Riding type: amateur and pro motocross racing.

records.statement: KTM and Husqvarna schedule a new piston at the minor engine service every 50 operating hours, with valves and con-rod at the major service every 100 hours. In real use, testers and parts dealers put a 250F piston at about 25-40 hours for an amateur racer and a 450F at about 30-60 hours, with some 450 pistons run 100 hours as a gamble; a pro should change a 450 piston by about 20 hours. Owners racing at local level report 30-50 hours. Riding type: pro race vs amateur race; trail riders are not covered and often go longer. Measure ring gap, skirt and bore rather than assume.

records.statement: KTM and Husqvarna schedule a valve-clearance check after the first hour, then every 30 operating hours. Mechanics and owners widely agree that a valve clearance that keeps getting tighter means the valve face or seat is wearing (titanium intakes most often), that the time between adjustments then gets shorter, and that the lasting fix is new valves with the seats cut, usually new springs too, rather than repeated shims. Riding type: all; dirty air filters and running on the rev limiter speed it up.

values.maker_interval: a valve-clearance check after the first hour, then every 30 operating hours
values.sign: clearance moving tighter at each check; hard starting

source.name: Vital MX forum, Drastic valve adjustment (KX450)

records.notes: A valve maker also recommends a complete new valve and spring kit for engines at or past factory service limits.

records.statement: KTM and Husqvarna schedule a fork service after 10 hours, then every 40 hours, and a shock service after 20 hours, then every 40 hours. A suspension columnist services a hard-ridden practice bike every 10-15 hours, while a European suspension dealer quotes 20-40 hours depending on the bike; both say sand, hard riding and fast riders shorten it. Oil is usually the last thing to wear; bushings, seals, piston bands and shims go first. Signs: you keep going stiffer and slower on the clickers and they do less. Riding type: race and practice.

values.maker_interval: a fork service after 10 hours, then every 40 hours, and a shock service after 20 hours, then every 40 hours

records.topic: how often riders clean the air filter
records.statement: KTM and Husqvarna schedule cleaning the air filter after every race. Most racers clean or swap the filter every ride day, many treat it as cheap insurance against valve and top-end wear, and some run 2-3 rides in clean conditions or use a filter skin; oil drying out or draining to the bottom of the foam is a reason to service it even when it looks clean. Riding type: race and practice; dust shortens it to every moto.

values.real_world: every ride day; 2-3 rides only in clean air
values.maker_interval: cleaning the air filter after every race

records.topic: owner-reported piston life on the KTM-group 450
records.statement: KTM and Husqvarna schedule a new piston at the minor engine service every 50 operating hours, with valves and con-rod at the major service every 100 hours.
